slides.subhead: What a countertop garden system actually needs — light, water, tray, and when a kit beats jars for apartment c
slides.narration: Countertop garden systems — kits vs DIY for apartments. The Sill Garden answer for a small apartment, without buying more equipment than you need.

slides.headline:
Match the setup
to your space.
slides.subhead: Light, noise, and spill risk matter more than pod count.
slides.narration: Start with usable space, daylight, and a tray that protects the rental surface. Then pick the smallest setup that still grows what you cook.

slides.headline:
Don't buy the
biggest kit first.
slides.subhead: Weak light is not a watering problem.
slides.narration: Skip the largest system until the plants prove they need it. Stretching stems usually mean more light, not more water.

slides.headline:
Start small.
Prove the routine.
slides.subhead: A real countertop system is light + water + drip control — not just a pretty pot. Buy a 3–6 pod kit if you want herbs with almost no learnin
slides.narration: Our verdict: A real countertop system is light + water + drip control — not just a pretty pot. Buy a 3–6 pod kit if you want herbs with almost no learning curve; use jars + clip light if budget and silence come first. Full guide on Sill Garden dot com.
